subtitle: Weather in °F and °C at once
promotionalText: Every temperature in °F and °C at once. Up to 20 cities or where you are, the next 24 hours and 10 days, rain map, air quality and severe weather alerts.
whatsNew:
A fresh look and a lot more weather:

• A new icon, and tiles with a touch of colour and small graphics: a wind compass, the sun's path, cloud at each height, and today against normal
• Sunrise and sunset colour: how good the next one is likely to look
• Visibility in miles and kilometres, or feet and metres in fog
• Swipe left and right between days in a day's details
• Widgets on the city's sky; tap one to open that city
• Each city opens at the top when you come back to it
• Small spacing and layout refinements throughout
description:
Two Degrees shows the weather in Fahrenheit and Celsius at the same time, so you never have to convert again. Pick which unit is large; the other is always right beside it.

YOUR CITIES
• Swipe between up to 20 cities, each on its own sky
• Use My Location to add the weather where you are (optional; you can say no)
• Search any place in the world, reorder, and swipe a city away

THE FORECAST
• Right now: temperature in °F and °C, condition, and today's high and low in both units
• The next 24 hours, with rain chances and a one-line summary ("Rain likely around 5 PM")
• Rain in the next two hours, and a rain map with live radar
• A 10-day forecast on one shared scale; tap a day for its hours, rain and wind
• Feels like, humidity and dew point, wind and gusts, UV, visibility, cloud cover and the moon
• Air quality and pollen, and how today compares with the usual and the records
• How colourful the next sunrise and sunset are likely to be

SEVERE WEATHER
• Warnings, watches and advisories from the US National Weather Service, most serious first
• Optional notifications for new alerts and rain starting soon (off unless you turn them on)

WIDGETS
• Small, medium and large Home Screen widgets
• Lock Screen widgets: a line above the clock, a circle, and a rectangle
• Use your Two Degrees cities, or give each widget a city of its own

MADE TO BE READ
• Follows your iPhone's text size, with its own size and font options too
• Full VoiceOver support: every reading is spoken in both units

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no ads, no tracking. Your cities stay on your iPhone. Only their locations are sent to get the weather; if you use My Location, it's rounded to about a kilometre first.

Made by Bradley Cowdrey. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, alerts from the US National Weather Service, radar from RainViewer, maps from OpenFreeMap.

Also on the Mac, with the weather in your menu bar and Dock: bradcowdrey.com/two-degrees
reviewNotes:
Two Degrees shows every temperature in both °F and °C at once. It is free, with no account, login, in-app purchases, ads, analytics, tracking or user-generated content. No demo account or sample files are needed.

FIRST LAUNCH
1. Agree to the terms (also at bradcowdrey.com/legal and in ⋯ > Terms & Privacy).
2. The app then shows one screen, "Show the weather where you are?", explaining Use My Location, with a single Continue button that leads to the standard iOS When In Use location request, where the choice is made (Allow or Don't Allow). If location is not allowed, the app works fully: it opens on New York, London and Tokyo and you can search for and add any city. Use My Location can be turned on or off later in ⋯ (top right of the city list). Location is requested only while the app is in use, at about 1 km accuracy, and the coordinates are rounded to 0.01° before they are used.

MAIN FEATURES
Swipe left and right between cities. Tap the large temperature to swap which unit is large. Tap the list button (bottom right) for all cities: search to add one (up to 20), swipe a card left to remove, ⋯ > Edit List to reorder. Scroll a city page for the hourly and 10-day forecast, the next 2 hours of rain, the Rain Map, air quality and pollen, sunrise/sunset colour, normals and records, and severe weather alerts when any are active. Widgets: Home Screen > Edit > Add Widget > Two Degrees; Lock Screen > Customize.

NOTIFICATIONS (OFF BY DEFAULT)
Nothing is asked at launch. In the city list, ⋯ > Notifications has two toggles: Severe Weather and Rain Starting Soon. Turning one on shows the iOS notification prompt. They are local notifications for My Location (or the first city); there is no push server.

SEVERE WEATHER ALERTS: UNITED STATES ONLY
Alerts come from the US National Weather Service (api.weather.gov) and exist only for US locations. Outside the US, or when nothing is active, no alert card is shown; this is expected, not a fault. To see the feature, add a US city that currently has an active alert (alerts.weather.gov lists them); an alert card appears at the top of its page, and tapping it opens the full NWS text. The app states that it is not a safety tool and that official warnings should be followed.

BACKGROUND APP REFRESH
Background App Refresh (BGAppRefreshTask "com.bradcowdrey.twodegrees.refresh", UIBackgroundModes "fetch") is scheduled only when at least one notification toggle is on. It refreshes the forecast and alerts so the rain and severe weather notifications can be posted. It does not use location in the background.

RAIN MAP
The Rain Map card opens our own web page (bradleycowdrey.github.io/two-degrees/radar.html) in a web view, showing RainViewer radar on OpenFreeMap map tiles for the city. It has no login or purchases; its only links are the RainViewer and OpenFreeMap credits.

DATA SOURCES (no keys, accounts or payments)
- Open-Meteo: forecast, city search, air quality and pollen (pollen is Europe only), and the historical archive for normals and records. CC BY 4.0, credited in the app.
- US National Weather Service: severe weather alerts (US only).
- RainViewer: radar images in the Rain Map.
- OpenFreeMap (OpenStreetMap data): map tiles in the Rain Map.
- GeoNames: a city list bundled in the app (used offline, no network calls). CC BY 4.0, credited in the app.
- Apple CLGeocoder: names the place for Use My Location.
Only a city's coordinates (rounded to 0.01°) are sent to these services; no personal data is collected, and the developer runs no server that receives or stores data.

REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
Forecasts work worldwide. Severe weather alerts are US only; pollen is Europe only; air quality uses US AQI in the US and European AQI elsewhere.

REGULATED INDUSTRY / THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL
Not applicable. Third-party data is used under its licenses and credited in the app.

mac.promotionalText: Every temperature in °F and °C at once, in your menu bar, Dock and desktop widgets. Up to 20 cities, the next 24 hours and 10 days, rain map and severe weather alerts.
mac.description:
Two Degrees shows the weather in Fahrenheit and Celsius at the same time, so you never have to convert again. Pick which unit is large; the other is always right beside it.

ON YOUR MAC
• In the menu bar: the temperature in both units, with the full panel one click away
• In the Dock: the icon shows the live reading on the sky, and a right-click lists every city
• Tear the panel off into its own window, keep it on top, and pick from five sizes
• Open at login, and press F or C to swap which unit is large

YOUR CITIES
• Up to 20 cities, each on its own sky, one click apart
• Use My Location to add the weather where you are (optional; you can say no)
• Search any place in the world, even offline, and reorder or rename your cities

THE FORECAST
• Right now: temperature in °F and °C, condition, and today's high and low in both units
• The next 24 hours, with rain chances and a one-line summary ("Rain likely around 5 PM")
• Rain in the next two hours, and a rain map with live radar
• A 10-day forecast on one shared scale; click a day for its hours, rain and wind
• Twelve detail tiles: feels like, humidity and dew point, wind with a compass, UV, visibility, precipitation, cloud at each height, the moon, air quality, sunrise and sunset, and today against normal
• How colourful the next sunrise and sunset are likely to be

SEVERE WEATHER
• Warnings, watches and advisories from the US National Weather Service, most serious first
• Optional notifications for new alerts and rain starting soon (off unless you turn them on)

WIDGETS
• Small, medium and large widgets for your desktop and Notification Center
• Each one can show your first city or a city of its own, with either unit large

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no ads, no tracking. Your cities stay on your Mac. Only their locations are sent to get the weather; if you use My Location, it's rounded to about a kilometre first.

Made by Bradley Cowdrey. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, alerts from the US National Weather Service, radar from RainViewer, maps from OpenFreeMap.

Also on iPhone and iPad, with Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets.
